title_refine.style: factual clickbait for China finance audience

entities.evidence: Public snippets confirm identity (co-founder of Centerview Partners, Democratic fundraiser) but none provide an established Simplified Chinese name; keep English label.
Only one non-official Chinese source (Zhihu) gives 森特尔维尤合伙公司; other Chinese pages keep the English name, so common_zh is low-confidence and title_label stays English.
CNBC and Wikipedia both describe Effron's donations going to Democratic candidates; 民主党筹款 is the standard rendering.
FEC and OpenSecrets both use 政治行动委员会 for PACs; transcript's 'packs' is a transcription of PACs.
CNBC and FEC coverage of 2022 races use 参议院选举/选战 for Senate races.
Ballotpedia and CNN confirm the Aug 2, 2022 Michigan Democratic primary; transcript's 'Elsaid' is a mis-transcription of Elissa Slotkin.

terms.sense: point at which spending stops yielding marginal returns

clip_research.source_claim: The cost of these races has gone up exponentially. A Senate race is going to be $200 million plus. A congressional race which used to be $5 million, $10 million to spend... the most money still comes from small-dollar donors... in Michigan, Elsaid against Stevens, there was a big difference in the money, but it didn't translate into the votes.
clip_research.public_baseline: 2022 federal and state races were expected to top $16.7 billion, the most expensive midterms ever (CNBC); FEC reports House and Senate candidates raised $3.1B and spent $2.7B through Sept 30, 2022.
clip_research.surprise_gap: Effron's $200M+ Senate-race figure and 'exponential' framing sit above the aggregate FEC candidate totals, suggesting much spending flows through outside groups/PACs rather than candidate committees; the Michigan example is a case where money did not decide the vote.

evidence.fact: Effron: Senate race costs $200M+; congressional race used to be $5-10M; most money still from small-dollar donors; Michigan money gap did not translate into votes.

data_driven_lessons.source: KC桌面-视频号动态数据明细.csv, 114 rows, July 2026 local analysis
winning_patterns: 机构/人物权威 + 具体数字/资产 + 强问题，例如 高盛王逸：4-5万亿城市更新会拖住楼市吗
大机构/名人 + 被逼/陷阱/真相/转向 等张力词，例如 野村辜朝明：日本央行被逼到墙角
具体数据 + 政策动作疑问，例如 6月PMI释放积极信号，政府会加码吗
反常识判断 + 下一步条件，例如 低估值可能是价值陷阱，需等待政策转向消费
中国相关议题更容易获得点击，但表达要落在政策、需求、信心、估值、产业升级这些正向框架
外资或海外权威给出对中国更积极的判断时，反差本身就是主标题，不要埋在摘要里
让观众产生单一强反应：居然如此、终于有人说、他说的是真的吗、原来中国优势在这里
大实话角度来自表达者身份与观点反差；言行反差角度必须有公开动作或披露支撑
涉及中国比较优势时，优先把外国企业被迫调整、海外权威改口或中国优势被低估写成冲突
avoid_patterns: 过长的新闻句，尤其是 24 字以上还塞多个从句
只有 策略/机会/影响/前瞻/市场/风险 这类泛词，没有具体对象或张力
美国宏观泛标题如果没有美联储/鲍威尔等强锚点，点击明显弱
纯描述式标题，例如 某市场短期风险与长期催化剂，缺少问题和冲突
经济危机/金融危机/崩盘/崩溃 这类过硬负面财经词
把事实换成疑问号但没有反差，例如 回报路径在哪、未来如何、能否实现
陌生英文人名或机构全称占据第一行，却没有告诉观众这个人为什么值得听
把 Bloomberg LP 等来源或公司法律后缀误当成采访对象
没有公开证据却暗示嘉宾撒谎、操纵或言行不一
